g.title: G
cluster_micro
cluster_meso
cluster_macro

p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward A higher exposure hazard in an age band raises the per-agent probability that a susceptible member of that band transitions from not exposed to exposed at the next observed step, so band-level hazard can drive individual new-exposure events.

p1_meso_band_attack_ratio → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward A higher cumulative attack ratio in an age band depletes susceptibles, which lowers the per-susceptible exposure hazard; an individual in that band is therefore less likely to show a new exposure transition.

p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward Cross-band inequality in exposure hazard can concentrate exposure pressure on agents in high-hazard age bands, making an individual new-exposure transition more plausible for those agents.

p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p1_micro_ever_exposed_state downward Sustained dispersion of band-level hazard can make some agents accumulate exposure earlier and more often, changing their cumulative ever-exposed state.

p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p7_micro_exposure_step_index downward Unequal band hazards can shift the timing of first exposure for agents in over-represented bands, moving their first observed exposure step index.

p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion → p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag downward Persistent cross-band hazard inequality can leave some age bands with continuing exposure opportunity after the city trough, raising the chance of post-trough individual exposure transitions.

p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward Higher per-edge exposure incidence in a layer indicates more active transmission there, increasing the chance that a new exposure event is attributed to that layer rather than to another setting.

p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward If the household layer has high per-edge incidence, household transmission intensity is elevated, increasing the likelihood that an individual's new exposure is attributed to the household layer.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p2_micro_layer_beta_load downward Uneven degree distribution within a contact layer can place a subset of agents under much heavier contact-weight load, shaping their per-layer beta load.

p2_meso_layer_degree_dispersion → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward High within-layer degree inequality can overload tracing around high-degree nodes, plausibly delaying an individual agent’s known-contact-to-quarantine latency.

p2_meso_layer_active_run → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward A layer that has sustained consecutive active exposure steps creates a locally infectious setting, increasing the chance that an individual's new exposure is attributed to that layer through repeated opportunities for contact within it.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward Household dyads with more secondary events can raise the partner’s near-term exposure hazard, increasing the plausibility of an individual new-exposure transition.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag downward Dyad-level secondary activity increases the chance that an agent’s exposure in that dyad carries a resolvable source attribution.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward A household dyad with more attributed secondary exposures is a more active transmission pair, making household-attributed exposure more plausible for its members.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p5_micro_known_contact_flag downward More secondary activity in a household dyad can trigger contact tracing for dyad members, making known-contact flagging more plausible.
p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward Repeated secondary exposure events within a household dyad can increase the chance that members are quarantined.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward When attributed secondary exposures are unevenly spread across household dyads, individuals in high-concentration dyads face stronger within-dyad exposure pressure, making a household-attributed exposure more likely for those agents.

p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward As a larger fraction of household-layer dyads accumulates attributed exposure, household transmission becomes more saturated; an individual exposure is then more likely to be recorded in the household-attributed category rather than in other settings.

p4_meso_group_silent_share → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag downward A higher silent share within a quarantine-status group can reflect weaker detection and behavioural visibility in that group, increasing the likelihood that a currently infectious group member remains undiagnosed and therefore silent.

p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward A quarantine-status group with high exposure yield per silent infectious person-step exerts greater transmission pressure on its members, raising the probability that an individual in that group shows a new exposure transition.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_micro_known_contact_flag downward A higher per-edge rate of known-contact transitions means contact tracing is yielding more flagged contacts in that layer, raising the probability that an individual agent becomes a known contact.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward When a layer generates many known-contact transitions per edge, tracing workload in that setting may rise, delaying the known-contact-to-quarantine interval for individual agents.

p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward Higher known-contact incidence per edge in a layer means more contacts are flagged and subsequently quarantined, raising the probability that an individual in that layer is quarantined.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration downward Tracing workload can prolong the time an infectious agent remains undiagnosed, plausibly extending individual silent-infectious duration.
p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_micro_known_contact_flag downward Heavy layer-level index load can make contact flagging less complete or slower, affecting an individual’s known-contact state.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward Higher per-index contact load in a layer can delay tracing work for individual contacts, increasing their known-contact-to-quarantine latency.

p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward When per-index contact load is high, quarantine decisions for individual contacts can be delayed or missed, altering individual quarantine status.

p5_meso_layer_load_dispersion → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward When per-index contact load is unevenly distributed across layers, tracing effort concentrates in high-load settings, delaying the known-contact-to-quarantine interval for individuals whose contacts lie in those congested layers.

p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward High dispersion of contact degree among quarantined agents implies a heavy lower tail of very low-contact behaviour; an individual quarantined agent is then more likely to fall into the fully suppressed zero-contact category.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward Stronger layer-level degree suppression under quarantine means quarantined agents in that layer have relatively fewer contacts, mechanically lowering their individual quarantined-to-non-quarantined contact ratio.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta downward Stronger layer-level suppression makes the quarantined-minus-non-quarantined degree difference more negative for agents in that layer, because quarantined agents reduce contacts more strongly.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward A higher suppression ratio indicates quarantined agents in the layer achieve lower contact degrees, increasing the chance that an individual quarantined agent records zero contacts.

p7_meso_layer_exposure_share → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward When a layer carries a larger share of attributed exposures, an individual’s exposure is more likely to be attributed to that active setting.

p7_meso_layer_exposure_share → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward A higher household layer share of attributed exposures makes household-attributed exposure more plausible for individual agents.
p7_meso_layer_exposure_share → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward Exposure concentration in a traced setting can increase quarantine actions for individuals linked to that setting.

p7_meso_band_share_drift → p7_micro_exposure_step_index downward Drift in an age band's share of exposures indicates a changing cohort timing pattern, which can shift when individual agents in that band first experience an observed exposure transition.

p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag downward A layer with elevated post-trough attributed exposure incidence increases the probability that an individual active in that layer experiences a new exposure transition after the city-wide infectious trough.

p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough downward When a band's post-trough incidence is much higher than at the trough, its exposures concentrate later in the resurgent phase, increasing the positive offset from the trough for individuals in that band.

p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio → p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag downward A higher band-level post-trough incidence ratio means exposure activity in that age band is elevated after the trough, raising the probability that an individual in the band has a post-trough exposure transition.

p1_macro_band_attack_range → p1_meso_band_hazard_dispersion downward A wide cross-age range in cumulative attack can signal uneven depletion and behavioural adaptation across age bands, which can reshape how exposure hazard is dispersed among bands in later steps rather than merely restating the aggregate range.

p1_macro_band_composition_mismatch → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard downward When exposure shares are misaligned with susceptible person-time, exposure pressure is disproportionately borne by bands with more remaining susceptible person-time; this can elevate the measured hazard in those bands as susceptible depletion and exposure targeting co-evolve.

p2_macro_layer_edge_turnover → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge downward High edge-set turnover breaks contact continuity within a setting, reducing the chance that any recorded edge repeatedly carries transmission and thereby lowering attributed exposure incidence per edge in that layer.

p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward When exposures are more evenly distributed across layers (higher entropy), the probability that a given new exposure is attributed to any particular layer falls, because no layer dominates the exposure mix.

p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward Lower entropy (concentrated exposure in few layers) often reflects household-dominated transmission, which increases the probability that an individual exposure is household-attributed; higher entropy reduces it.

p2_macro_layer_incidence_entropy → p2_meso_layer_active_run downward Higher entropy means exposure activity is spread across more contact layers; this dilution reduces the likelihood that any single layer sustains consecutive active exposure steps, shortening its active run.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward A higher population-level household share increases the chance that any individual new exposure is attributed to the household layer, because household transmission is a larger component of the force of infection.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward When household transmission dominates, quarantined agents may retain more household contacts relative to non-quarantined agents, increasing their individual contact ratio because household contacts are less easily suspended.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count downward A larger household share of all exposures implies more transmission occurs within household dyads, raising the expected number of attributed secondary exposures per household dyad.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction downward As household-attributed transmission grows as a fraction of all exposures, a greater proportion of household dyads will accumulate at least one attributed exposure event.

p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag downward High concentration of dyad-level attribution can shift source-resolved exposure events toward a small set of agents, affecting individual attribution status.

p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward When attributed household exposures are concentrated in few dyads, agents in those high-count dyads face a higher chance of household-attributed exposure.
p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward Concentrated household-attributed clusters can generate more household contact quarantine around the affected dyads.

p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction downward Greater concentration of attributed secondary events can leave many dyads with no attribution, plausibly lowering the fraction of household dyads ever attacked.

p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share downward Household concentration of attributed secondary exposures can increase the household layer’s share of attributed exposure transitions.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag downward Higher detection coverage shortens the undiagnosed infectious period by finding cases sooner, reducing the probability that an infectious agent is silent (infectious but undiagnosed) at a sampled step.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p4_micro_symptomatic_undiagnosed_flag downward Increased detection coverage identifies symptomatic cases more quickly, lowering the chance that a symptomatic agent remains undiagnosed.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p5_micro_known_contact_flag downward Higher detection coverage means more index cases are identified, triggering contact tracing that flags a larger number of agents as known contacts.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward Higher detection coverage can increase the number of index cases, straining tracing capacity and lengthening the interval between known-contact flagging and quarantine for individual agents.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward More diagnoses per infectious person-step lead to more tracing and isolation actions, raising the probability that an individual agent enters quarantine.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward Higher detection coverage leads to more quarantine episodes; if quarantined agents comply strongly, their contact degree while quarantined falls, lowering the individual quarantined-to-non-quarantined ratio.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p4_meso_group_silent_share downward Higher detection coverage reduces the fraction of infectious person-steps that are undiagnosed within quarantine-status groups, because more infections are diagnosed.

p4_macro_detection_coverage_rate → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate downward More diagnoses generate more contact-tracing actions per contact edge in each layer, increasing the rate of known-contact transitions per edge.

p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward A higher silent share implies more undetected infectious contact, plausibly raising an individual’s chance of a new exposure transition.

p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share → p5_micro_known_contact_flag downward A larger silent infectious pool can reduce recognition of source cases, making it less likely that an individual is flagged as a known contact.

p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share → p5_micro_tracing_latency downward Silent transmission can delay source identification and contact notification, plausibly lengthening an individual known-contact-to-quarantine interval.

p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward When more infectious activity is undiagnosed, contact-triggered quarantine can become less frequent for individuals linked to undetected sources.
p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard downward Undetected infectious activity can maintain exposure pressure in age bands, plausibly raising band-level exposure hazard.

p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge downward Silent infectious agents can generate layer-attributed exposures without diagnosis, plausibly increasing attributed incidence per layer edge.
p4_macro_silent_prevalence_share → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate downward A larger undiagnosed infectious pool can reduce known-contact transitions per recorded edge within a layer.

p4_macro_masking_ratio → p4_meso_group_silent_share downward A large accumulated pool of never-diagnosed ever-exposed agents can feed back into group-level silent infectious activity by sustaining undetected transmission within quarantine-status groups.

p4_macro_symptom_to_diagnosis_lag → p4_micro_silent_infectious_duration downward A longer population-average symptom-to-diagnosis interval implies diagnosis occurs later in the disease course, extending the period during which an individual can remain infectious while undiagnosed.

p5_macro_traced_per_diagnosis → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load downward When more known contacts are generated per new diagnosis, each index case implies more layer-specific contact investigations, increasing the per-index contact load that must be examined within contact layers.

p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p5_micro_quarantine_flag downward When average tracing latency is long, quarantine starts later for newly flagged contacts, reducing the probability that an individual is already quarantined at a given step.

p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward Delayed quarantine shortens the effective period of contact reduction, so an individual's contact degree while quarantined may be less reduced relative to their non-quarantine degree, increasing the ratio.

p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate downward Longer tracing latency slows the conversion of contact edges into known-contact transitions, lowering the per-edge rate of known-contact incidence in each layer.

p5_macro_mean_tracing_latency → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio downward Longer average tracing latency delays quarantine onset, so quarantined agents have less time under contact suppression; this raises the layer-level degree suppression ratio (less suppression).

p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward Broader quarantine coverage removes more potential transmitters from social contact, plausibly reducing an individual’s chance of a new exposure transition.

p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward Higher population quarantine coverage can reduce layer-attributed exposure opportunities for individuals in affected contact settings.

p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward If quarantined index cases are isolated away from households earlier, household-attributed exposure becomes less plausible for their members.

p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p4_micro_silent_infectious_flag downward Higher quarantine coverage can remove diagnosed or traced individuals from circulation, changing which infectious agents remain silently undiagnosed.

p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward Widespread quarantine coverage can reinforce norms and operational support for staying home, increasing the chance a quarantined agent records zero contacts.
p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge downward Broader quarantine coverage can reduce transmission per remaining layer edge by removing infectious contacts from settings.
p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count downward More quarantine coverage can reduce household dyad secondary exposure events by shortening infectious contact within households.

p5_macro_quarantine_coverage → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share downward Quarantine coverage can differentially suppress exposures in settings with many traced contacts, shifting the layer composition of attributed exposures.

p5_macro_known_contact_prevalence → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load downward A higher standing known-contact prevalence increases operational tracing caseload, which can raise the per-index contact load that must be examined within specific layers as newly quarantined agents are processed.
p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward A population-wide decline in contact volume reduces opportunities for individual exposure transitions; an increase raises them.
p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p2_micro_layer_degree downward Changes in aggregate contact volume can directly alter the number of layer edges incident to an individual agent.
p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p2_micro_layer_beta_load downward When total contact volume changes, an individual’s summed per-layer contact weights can change through added or removed edges.

p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward Population contact-volume shifts change the baseline contact environment against which a quarantined agent’s contact reduction is measured.

p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward A large population contact decline can make it more likely that a quarantined individual records no contact edges at a step.
p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p7_micro_exposure_step_index downward Contact-volume changes alter when individuals first meet infectious contacts, shifting an agent’s first observed exposure step.

p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge downward Aggregate contact volume change alters the density and edge turnover of settings, plausibly changing layer-attributed exposure incidence per edge.
p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count downward When total contact volume falls, household dyad exposure events can decrease; when it rises, secondary counts can increase.
p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p5_meso_layer_index_contact_load downward Changes in overall contact volume alter the per-index contact load that must be examined within a layer during tracing.

p6_macro_adherence_share → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward A larger population share of quarantined agents contacting at or below the non-quarantined median can reinforce adherence norms, increasing the probability that an individual quarantined agent records zero contacts at a step.

p6_macro_population_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward A lower population-level quarantine suppression ratio indicates stronger overall activity reduction among quarantined agents, shaping the adherence context in which an individual quarantined agent’s own in-quarantine contact ratio is realised.

p7_macro_age_composition_drift → p7_micro_exposure_step_index downward As the age composition of incident exposures drifts toward groups that were less affected earlier, individual agents in those newly affected age groups tend to have later first observed exposure step indices.

p7_macro_layer_composition_drift → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward High composition drift means the dominant exposure settings are changing, so an individual exposure is less likely to be attributed to the original dominant layer and more likely to newly important layers.

p7_macro_layer_composition_drift → p2_meso_layer_active_run downward When the layer composition of exposures drifts, transmission shifts between settings, disrupting sustained activity in any one layer and shortening its consecutive active-exposure run.

p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward A shift in the aggregate exposure growth regime after quarantine onset changes the background exposure pressure on individuals.
p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine → p7_micro_exposure_step_index downward Growth-regime change can accelerate or delay individual first exposures, shifting the observed exposure step index.

p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine → p1_meso_band_exposure_hazard downward A change in exposure growth regime around first quarantine onset can alter which age bands retain exposure pressure, shifting band-level hazard.
p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge downward Growth-regime change after quarantine onset can reduce or redirect layer-specific exposure events per edge.

p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count downward If the growth regime shifts at first quarantine, household dyad secondary exposure counts can respond through changed household contact and isolation.

p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine → p4_meso_group_exposure_yield_silent downward A post-quarantine growth shift can change how many exposures are generated per silent infectious person-step in quarantine-status groups.

p7_macro_growth_change_at_first_quarantine → p5_meso_layer_known_contact_rate downward Growth-regime change after quarantine onset can alter tracing yield per layer edge by changing case volume and contact patterns.

p7_macro_median_age_of_new_exposures → p7_meso_band_exposure_share downward A shift in the median age of new exposures can trigger age-targeted intervention and behavioural responses, redistributing subsequent exposure transitions across age-band shares rather than being a mere composition identity.

p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth → p1_micro_new_exposure_flag downward A stronger post-trough resurgence increases the background force of infection, making individual new-exposure transitions more plausible.

p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth → p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag downward When city-wide infectious growth after the trough is stronger, individual exposure transitions are more likely to occur after the trough.
p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth → p2_meso_layer_incidence_per_edge downward Resurgent infectious activity after the trough can increase layer-attributed exposure incidence per recorded edge.
p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count downward Higher post-trough growth can generate more household dyad secondary exposure events as transmission resumes.

p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio downward Stronger post-trough infectious growth can raise layer-specific post-trough exposure incidence relative to the trough, increasing the layer rebound ratio.

p8_macro_post_trough_infectious_growth → p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio downward Post-trough growth can be age-selective, plausibly raising the after-versus-at-trough exposure hazard ratio in some age bands.

p8_macro_resurgence_amplitude → p8_meso_layer_post_trough_incidence_ratio downward A larger citywide post-trough rebound implies stronger re-activation of transmission opportunities, which can differentially raise attributed exposure incidence in specific contact layers after the trough.

p8_macro_trough_susceptible_depletion → p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio downward Greater susceptible depletion at the trough leaves fewer susceptible person-steps in each age band, reducing the post-trough rebound ratio of band exposure hazard relative to its trough value.

p8_macro_resurgence_breadth → p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag downward Widespread layer resurgence increases transmission in multiple settings, raising the chance that an individual new exposure is attributed to one of the resurging layers.

p8_macro_resurgence_breadth → p8_micro_offset_from_infectious_trough downward Widespread resurgence extends post-trough exposure activity, so agents exposed during rebound tend to have larger positive offsets from the trough step.

p8_macro_resurgence_breadth → p8_micro_post_trough_exposure_flag downward Broader layer resurgence increases the overall post-trough exposure pressure, raising the probability that an individual new exposure occurs after the infectious trough.

p8_macro_resurgence_breadth → p2_meso_layer_active_run downward Resurgence across many layers re-activates multiple contact settings, increasing the consecutive active-exposure run length observed in those layers after the trough.

p8_macro_resurgence_breadth → p7_meso_layer_exposure_share downward Broad resurgence across many layers shifts exposure shares toward the resurging settings, increasing their layer exposure share at the resurgence stage.

p8_macro_resurgence_breadth → p8_meso_band_post_trough_incidence_ratio downward When resurgence is broad across many layers, post-trough exposure activity is more widespread, raising band-specific post-trough incidence ratios relative to the trough.

N1 | p1_micro_new_exposure_flag Agent new-exposure transition indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: age_structured_incidence_divergence Definition: X_i(t) = 1 if exposed_i(t) = true and exposed_i(t-1) = false, otherwise 0; defined only when agent i is observed at both step t and the immediately preceding observed step t-1 in the same run; undefined if either observation is missing. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N2 | p1_micro_ever_exposed_state Agent cumulative ever-exposed indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: age_structured_incidence_divergence Definition: E_i(t) = max over observed steps s <= t in the same run of X_i(s), where X is the new-exposure transition indicator; E_i(t) = 1 if any such s has X_i(s) = 1, else 0; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N8 | p2_micro_layer_degree Agent contact degree within a contact layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: d_i,l(t) = number of distinct contact records at step t in layer l with agent_id = i plus those with partner_id = i, de-duplicated by unordered pair so that a reciprocal pair counts once; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N9 | p2_micro_layer_exposure_flag Agent exposure transition attributed to a layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: E_i,l(t) = 1 if X_i(t) = 1 and the layer recorded on the exposure event for that agent and step equals l; 0 if X_i(t) = 1 and the recorded layer is non-null and different from l; undefined if X_i(t) = 0, if the recorded layer is null, or if no exposure event can be matched. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N10 | p2_micro_layer_beta_load Agent per-layer contact weight load Scale: micro | Phenomenon: setting_specific_cluster_persistence Definition: W_i,l(t) = sum of beta over the undirected contact edges at step t in layer l incident to agent i; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N16 | p3_micro_household_degree Agent degree in the persistent household layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: d_i,H(t) = number of distinct undirected contact pairs at step t in layer l_H incident to agent i; l_H is the layer value with the largest mean consecutive-step Jaccard overlap of its edge set over all observed steps in the run; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. Execution: {'3249f90463154305aed53504106b3dae': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}
